en: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: A woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have a daughter who is a newlywed and she contracted measles, so her hair fell out; may I attach hair extensions to it?" He said: "May Allah curse the woman who adds hair extensions and the woman who asks for them."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Madani narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Hisham—meaning Ibn Sa'd; both from Zayd ibn Aslam, with this chain of narration.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Beware of sitting in the pathways." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we cannot do without our gatherings where we converse." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "If you refuse but to gather, then give the road its due right." They said: "And what is its right?" He said: "Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning greetings of peace, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong."

And Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Madani informed us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated it to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: Hisham—meaning Ibn Sa'd—informed us; both from Zayd ibn Aslam, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Beware of sitting in the pathways." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we cannot do without our gatherings where we converse." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "So if you refuse but to gather, then give the road its due right." They said: "And what is its right?" He said: "Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning greetings of peace, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong."

And Muhammad ibn Rafi', Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub (H). And Abu Ja'far al-Darimi narrated to us: Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with that.

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Uthman ibn Uthman al-Ghatafani narrated to us: Umar ibn Nafi' narrated to us (H). And Umayyah ibn Bistam narrated to me: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us, from Umar ibn Nafi', with the chain of Ubayd Allah, the like of it, and they both incorporated the explanation into the hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us (H). And Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us; they said: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of Abu Usamah, he made the explanation from the words of Ubayd Allah.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id—narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah: Umar ibn Nafi' informed me, from his father, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade al-qaza'. He said: I said to Nafi': "What is al-qaza'?" He said: "Shaving part of a boy's head and leaving part of it."

Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I saw the branding iron in the hand of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was branding the camels of zakah.

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah: Hisham ibn Zayd narrated to me, he said: I heard Anas saying: We entered upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in an enclosure while he was branding sheep. He said: I think he said: on their ears. And Yahya ibn Habib narrated it to me: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad, Yahya, and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Anas narrating that when his mother gave birth, they set off with the infant to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for him to perform tahnik for him. He said: And behold, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in an enclosure branding sheep. Shu'bah said: To the best of my knowledge, he said: on their ears.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi Adi narrated to me, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad, from Anas, who said: When Umm Sulaym gave birth, she said to me: "O Anas, watch this boy, and let nothing touch him until you take him in the morning to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) so that he may perform tahnik for him." He said: So I went in the morning, and behold, he was in the walled garden wearing a dark cloak, branding the camels that had been brought to him during the Conquest.

Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Na'im Abu Abd Allah, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated to him that he heard Ibn Abbas saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw a donkey branded on the face, and he denounced that. Ibn Abbas said: "By Allah, I will not brand it except on the part farthest from the face." So he ordered a donkey of his, and it was branded on its haunches; and he was the first to brand the haunches.

And Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that a donkey that had been branded on its face passed by the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), whereupon he said: "May Allah curse the one who branded it."

And Harun ibn Abd Allah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us (H). And Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bakr informed us; both from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade striking the face and branding on the face.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from Abbad ibn Tamim, that Abu Bashir al-Ansari informed him that he was with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on one of his journeys. He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent a messenger—Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr said: I think he said: while the people were in their resting places—saying: "Let no bowstring necklace or any necklace remain around the neck of a camel except that it is cut off." Malik said: "I see that this was because of the evil eye."

And Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Ismail—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The bell is the wind-instrument of Satan."
And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us (H). And Qutaybah narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz—meaning al-Darawardi—narrated to us; both from Suhayl, with this chain of narration.

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari narrated to us: Bishr—meaning Ibn Mufaddal—narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The angels do not accompany a traveling party that has a dog or a bell."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The angels do not enter a house in which there are statues or images."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and their wordings are close—they said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: I entered with Abu Hurayrah into the house of Marwan, and he saw images in it. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And who is more unjust than one who sets about creating a creation like My creation? Let them create an ant, or let them create a grain, or let them create a barley corn." And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: Abu Hurayrah and I entered a house being built in Medina for Sa'id or Marwan. He said: And he saw an artist making images in the house, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said the like of it, and he did not mention: "or let them create a barley corn."

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, they said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, that a man came to Ibn Abbas; and he mentioned from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) the like of it.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas ibn Malik, who said: I was sitting with Ibn Abbas while he was issuing fatwas without saying 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said,' until a man asked him, saying: "I am a man who makes these images." Ibn Abbas said to him: "Come closer." So the man drew closer, and Ibn Abbas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Whoever makes an image in this world will be tasked to breathe a soul into it on the Day of Resurrection, and he will never be able to breathe it in."

And Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Mansur narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Subayh, who said: I was with Masruq in a house that contained statues of Mary. Masruq said: "These are statues of Khosrow." I said: "No, these are statues of Mary." Masruq said: "Behold, I heard Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: The people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are the image-makers." Muslim said: I read to Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami from Abd al-A'la ibn Abd al-A'la: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "I am a man who makes these images, so give me a ruling concerning them." He said to him: "Come closer to me." So he drew closer to him, then he said: "Come closer to me." So he drew closer until he placed his hand upon his head and said: "I will inform you of what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: Every image-maker will be in the Fire; for every image he made, a soul will be created for it to punish him in Hell." And he said: "If you must do so, then make trees and that which has no soul." Nasr ibn Ali confirmed it.

And Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, all of them from Abu Mu'awiyah (H). And Ibn Abi Umar narrated it to us: Sufyan narrated to us; both from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration. And in the narration of Yahya and Abu Kurayb from Abu Mu'awiyah: "Indeed, among the people of the Fire most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are the image-makers." And the hadith of Sufyan is like the hadith of Waki'.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash (H). And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to me: Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are the image-makers." And al-Ashajj did not mention 'Indeed' (Inna).

Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated to us, they said: Hammad narrated to us (H). And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail—meaning Ibn Ulayyah—narrated to us (H). And Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: al-Thaqafi narrated to us; all of them from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of Ubayd Allah from Nafi' from Ibn Umar from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us (H). And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya—namely al-Qattan—narrated to us; both from Ubayd Allah (H). And Ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his: My father narrated to us: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', that Ibn Umar informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Those who make images will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them: Bring to life that which you created."
